subject: Hosted API: simplify DPA/subprocessor phrasing for customer portal
messages:
From: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmerobotics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask on DPA/subprocessors for procurement docs

Hi Rishi (and Laura),

Thanks for the call earlier — procurement asked me to follow up with a couple of concrete items we need before we can move to legal review:

- A plain-language summary (1-2 sentences) that we can paste into our SOW and vendor checklist describing what Redwood does with customer data when using the Hosted API.
- Confirmation of whether the subprocessor list is the latest and a snapshot we can attach to our internal security questionnaire (they prefer a CSV or similar).
- Clarify whether any subprocessors transfer data outside the U.S. and what safeguards are in place (standard contractual clauses / EU SCCs, or equivalent).

Can you point me to a short blurb and the latest subprocessor file? Procurement is on a tight timeline this week.

Thanks,
Sara Jones
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme Robotics

--

Sara — thanks, noted. Looping in Laura (legal) and Vanessa (product copy) to produce a short, customer-facing snippet and an attachable subprocessor CSV.

Proposed plan:
1) Laura to confirm legal-safe plain-language text we can publish in the Console and hand to procurement.
2) Vanessa to draft a 1–2 sentence summary optimized for procurement checklists and the Console "Data handling" tooltip.
3) I will attach the latest subprocessor snapshot and SCC summary once Laura confirms.

Vanessa/Laura — can you take this as a quick turn? Procurement needs a copy they can include with their vendor packet by end of day tomorrow. If legal prefers to redact anything from the CSV, call it out and we'll provide a redacted snapshot and a note explaining why.

Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmerobotics.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on DPA/subprocessors for procurement docs

Thanks Rishi. Vanessa — draft below is my legal-approved plain-language version and guidance for the CSV. Sara — sharing here so procurement can see the exact wording and the attachments we plan to send.

Plain-language blurb (legal-approved):
"Redwood Inference processes customer data only to provide Hosted API services. We do not use customer content to train or improve models. A list of subprocessors we engage for service delivery (e.g., cloud providers, observability vendors) is maintained and available on request; we provide a dated snapshot for procurement and audit purposes."

Notes / clarifications:
- Subprocessor snapshot: we will provide the latest CSV with vendor name, role, country of processing, and date of record. If a vendor entry contains contract-level details we consider confidential, we will provide a redacted entry and a short note explaining the redaction.
- Cross-border transfers: where subprocessors process data outside the customer region, we rely on SCCs or equivalent transfer mechanisms and have documented safeguards; we can provide the SCC summary doc on request.
- Hosted API specifics: include the Console tooltip copy that Vanessa drafts; we recommend keeping the SOW snippet focused on high-level commitments and linking to the DPA for detailed terms.

Attachments (attached to this thread): Redwood_DPA_summary_v2.pdf, subprocessor_map_snapshot.csv

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jones <sara.jones@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick ask on DPA/subprocessors for procurement docs

Sara — attaching the two files Laura referenced and a short console-friendly sentence Vanessa prepared below. Please confirm if this is acceptable for procurement or if you'd prefer an alternative phrasing. We can also provide the full SCC summary under an NDA if your legal team requires it.

Console / procurement snippet (suggested):
"Redwood processes customer requests to deliver Hosted API features. We maintain a dated list of subprocessors and will provide a snapshot for procurement; cross-border transfers are protected by standard contractual clauses or equivalent safeguards."

Attachments:
- Redwood_DPA_summary_v2.pdf (summary of key DPA clauses; 3 pages)
- subprocessor_map_snapshot.csv (vendor, role, country, recorded_at)

Next steps: please reply to confirm and we'll upload the CSV to the shared procurement drive and provide a Drive link and/or signed SCC checklist if needed.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
